en.title: Family Transformation
en.summary: PART XIV turns from the contemporary economy to contemporary social and cultural change. Chapter 132 begins with the family because households are the point at which demographic transition, migration, education, property, paid work, unpaid care, digital communication and social policy become everyday social relations. In Mithila, Vajji and Anga, however, ‘family transformation’ cannot be reduced to a simple story in which a traditional joint family disappears and a modern nuclear family replaces it.

mai.title: परिवारक रूपान्तरण
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “परिवारक रूपान्तरण” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Family and household: two units that must not be confused
The evidence problem after 2011 on the Indian side
Household size is changing, but not everywhere at the same rate
Nuclearisation is not a one-way historical law

en.title: Changing Marriage Practices
en.summary: Chapter 133 examines changing marriage practices as a social institution, a household strategy and a legal relationship. Marriage in Mithila, Vajji and Anga is often discussed through ritual continuity, but the contemporary history lies equally in changing ages at marriage, education, migration, partner search, dowry and wedding expenditure, registration, post-marital residence, digital communication and the growing importance of individual consent.

mai.title: बदलैत विवाह-प्रथा
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “बदलैत विवाह-प्रथा” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Marriage as alliance, contract, mobility and household formation
Evidence architecture: surveys, censuses, law, registration and ethnography
The persistence of family-mediated partner search
Bihar: a measurable decline in marriage before eighteen

en.title: Gender, Education and Employment
en.summary: Chapter 134 examines a central paradox of contemporary social change in Mithila, Vajji and Anga: girls and women have made major gains in schooling and, in Bihar, female enrolment now matches or exceeds male enrolment at several educational levels, yet the conversion of education into secure paid work remains sharply unequal. Education, employment and gender cannot therefore be read as a simple sequence in which more years of schooling automatically produce economic independence.

mai.title: लैंगिकता, शिक्षा आ रोजगार
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “लैंगिकता, शिक्षा आ रोजगार” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Gender links household reproduction to the wider economy
Evidence architecture: enrolment, learning, credentials and labour measures are not interchangeable
Literacy change is generational, not instantaneous
Bihar has reached gender parity in school enrolment ratios before reaching high enrolment at every level

en.title: Youth Culture
en.summary: Chapter 135 examines youth culture as a social field created by education, work, migration, digital media, language, consumption, family expectations, public space and the unequal distribution of time and mobility. “Youth” is not a timeless stage with one fixed age boundary, and it does not describe a single homogeneous generation.

mai.title: युवा संस्कृति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “युवा संस्कृति” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Youth is a policy category as well as a life stage
India and Nepal institutionalise different boundaries of youth
Bihar still has an unusually large youth share, but the demographic peak is not permanent
Madhesh has a similarly youthful age structure, but its policy definition is wider

en.title: Social Media and Language
en.summary: Chapter 136 examines social media as a linguistic institution rather than merely a communications technology. Facebook, WhatsApp, YouTube, Instagram, short-video platforms, messaging groups and emerging AI-assisted interfaces now sit between speech, writing, performance, migration and public debate. They make some language forms easy to record and circulate, others easy to search, and still others difficult to type or discover. The result is not a simple shift from “offline” to “online” language.

mai.title: सोशल मीडिया आ भाषा
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “सोशल मीडिया आ भाषा” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Social media is now an infrastructure of everyday language change
Platforms do not simply carry pre-existing languages
The regional language field is multilingual before it becomes digital
Maithili has strong demographic presence but unequal digital resources across domains

en.title: Religious Change and Public Ritual
en.summary: Chapter 137 examines religious change through public ritual: the recurrent acts by which households, neighbourhoods, congregations, pilgrims, associations and public authorities occupy time and space together. It does not assume that religious change can be read directly from census percentages. Affiliation, belief, observance, institutional membership and participation in a festival are different variables.

mai.title: धार्मिक परिवर्तन आ सार्वजनिक अनुष्ठान
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “धार्मिक परिवर्तन आ सार्वजनिक अनुष्ठान” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: From religious affiliation to lived public religion
Why public ritual is a particularly sensitive indicator of social change
The scale of public religion is not the same as the size of a religious population
Chhath as a household vow transformed into shared public infrastructure

en.title: Caste in Contemporary Society
en.summary: Chapter 138 examines caste as a contemporary social institution rather than as an unchanged survival from the past. Caste can shape marriage choices, neighbourhood relations, land access, political organization, educational trajectories, occupational networks and claims on the state, but none of those outcomes follows automatically from a person’s jati or administrative category.

mai.title: समकालीन समाजमे जाति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “समकालीन समाजमे जाति” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Caste is contemporary because institutions keep remaking it
Jati, social category and legal status are different analytical objects
Bihar’s 2022–23 Caste-Based Survey changed the evidentiary landscape
The broad Bihar profile shows why “upper” and “backward” cannot be treated as small margins

en.title: Madhesh, Federalism and Social Citizenship
en.summary: Chapter 139 examines federalism through the everyday institutions that make citizenship usable. Madhesh was central to Nepal’s transition from a unitary state because movements in the Tarai-Madhesh linked regional identity and political inclusion to demands for state restructuring. The Constitution of 2015 created a three-tier federal democratic republic, and the eight districts from Saptari to Parsa now form Madhesh Province with Janakpurdham as its capital and 136 constitutionally recognized local governments.

mai.title: मधेश, संघीयता आ सामाजिक नागरिकता
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “मधेश, संघीयता आ सामाजिक नागरिकता” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Federalism is a question of social citizenship, not only territorial design
Madhesh is central to Nepal’s federal question because demands for inclusion preceded the province
The 2015 Constitution created three constitutionally recognized levels of government
The federal settlement answered some Madhesh demands while leaving other disputes alive

en.title: Maithili, Angika and Bajjika in Contemporary Public Life
en.summary: Chapter 140 examines Maithili, Angika and Bajjika as languages of contemporary public life rather than as timeless cultural labels. Public life includes census naming, constitutional status, administration, education, examinations, literary institutions, broadcasting, digital media, political mobilisation and everyday interaction with the state. The three names do not occupy the same institutional position.

mai.title: समकालीन सार्वजनिक जीवनमे मैथिली, अंगिका आ बज्जिका
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “समकालीन सार्वजनिक जीवनमे मैथिली, अंगिका आ बज्जिका” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Public life requires separating language, variety, script and legal status
The three names inhabit different recognition regimes
Maithili’s Eighth Schedule status created national institutional access
Constitutional recognition does not make Maithili Bihar’s routine administrative language

en.title: Cultural Heritage versus Living Culture
en.summary: Chapter 141 examines the tension between cultural heritage and living culture. The tension is real, but the opposition is often misleading. Heritage is not simply the old part of culture preserved from change, while living culture is not simply the new part left outside museums. Heritage is a process of selection, documentation, recognition and transmission through which some practices, objects, places and memories are made publicly valuable.

mai.title: सांस्कृतिक धरोहर बनाम जीवित संस्कृति
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “सांस्कृतिक धरोहर बनाम जीवित संस्कृति” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: Heritage is a process of selection, not a neutral storehouse
The UNESCO concept of living heritage rejects the idea of a frozen original
Safeguarding is different from conservation
Tangible and intangible heritage are interdependent

en.title: The Future of the Regional Cultural Economy
en.summary: Chapter 142 closes PART XIV by asking a deliberately economic question without reducing culture to merchandise: what would allow the cultural life of Mithila, Vajji and Anga to generate durable livelihoods, institutions and public value over the next decade? The answer cannot be a single market forecast.

mai.title: क्षेत्रीय सांस्कृतिक अर्थव्यवस्थाक भविष्य
mai.summary: ई अध्याय “क्षेत्रीय सांस्कृतिक अर्थव्यवस्थाक भविष्य” विषयक परिवार, विवाह, शिक्षा-रोजगार, युवा, सोशल मीडिया, धर्म, जाति, मधेश, भाषा आ जीवित संस्कृतिक स्रोत-आधारित ऐतिहासिक पड़ताल करैत अछि।

outline: The regional cultural economy is larger than the handicraft sector
No official dataset gives a single market size for Mithila, Vajji and Anga
Global creative-economy growth provides context, not a regional forecast
India’s ‘Orange Economy’ policy creates a new national opportunity structure
